Topic 'Arrays in Java (declare, create, initialize; indexing; length; default values)' of section 1.4 holds the concept off by one error.

[0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: an everyday new box is 'empty' (nothing in it), and C-trained intuition says new memory holds garbage. Java rule: every element of a new array holds a definite default (0 for numbers, 0.0 for double, false for boolean, null for String and other reference types).
[1] misconception (M) -> NewArrayHoldsGarbage: wrong rule: The slots of a new int[n] hold unpredictable values until assigned. Right rule: new fills every element with a default: 0 for numeric types, false for boolean, null for String and other non-primitive types.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> NewArrayHoldsGarbage: Points to LT: creation stores the default in every element before any statement can read one. Inconsistent application: the trace reads a fresh a[i] as 0 on one pass but as 'empty' or 'unknown' on another, or gives a new boolean[] the value true. (here mixing in: "The slots of a new int[n] hold unpredictable values until assigned")
[3] misconception (M) -> ArrayCreationIsFree: wrong rule: Creating a big array with new takes no time because the elements are not set yet. Right rule: Because Java sets every element to its default at creation, creating an array takes time proportional to its length.

[0] names_the_element (N): Identity: the initial value Java gives each element of a newly created array: zero for numeric types, false for boolean, null for references.
[1] states_the_rule (S): Declarative: 'The default initial value is zero for all numbers and false for type boolean'; for String and other non-primitive types it is null. The same holds for every entry of a 2-D array.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Sequencing: defaults are stored during creation, before the reference is returned. An explicit initialization loop that follows simply overwrites them, so the loop is needed only for a non-default start value.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Result: reading an element never assigned gives 0 in an int[], 0.0 in a double[], false in a boolean[] and null in a String[] (println prints the text null).
[2] one_step_execution (OS): State transition: the creation step sets all n element variables to the default in one go. Reading a default changes nothing.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Defaults come from creation, so every execution of new resets them; creating the array inside the trial loop gives each experiment a clean all-false grid.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): new boolean[n] starts every flag at false ('not seen yet'), so CouponCollector needs no initialization loop. PrimeSieve needs true as its start value and so must loop to set it.
[2] relation_to_neighbour (R): A local variable has no value until it is assigned: using it first is a compile-time error. An array element is given a default value (0, 0.0, false) when the array is created with new, so it can be read before any assignment.
[3] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Plan/role: lets counter and flag arrays (counts[], found[]) start at 0 or false, ready to accumulate, with no initialization loop; the book calls this using Java's default array initialization convention.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> NewArrayHoldsGarbage: Conservation: changing the element type changes the default (int 0, double 0.0, boolean false, String null). Moving the creation into a loop resets the defaults on each pass. Adding an explicit loop that stores the default changes nothing.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Applicability: rely on the defaults when the needed start value is exactly 0, 0.0, false or null (counters, flags, accumulators). Write an initialization loop for any other start value. Plain local variables get no default, so the convenience applies only to array elements.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Defaults are 0/false/null; any other start value must be assigned explicitly. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: the code assumes a non-default start value without setting it, e.g. PrimeSieve with its 'isPrime[i] = true' loop removed counts 0 primes
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Elements of a reference-type array start as null, which refers to no object. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: a method is called on an element of a new String[] (or other object array) before it is assigned, e.g. s[0].length() (NullPointerException)
